AWARD  Vide this award, the Tribunal shall decide the DAR treated as MACT claim petition bearing no. 440/19, under section 166(4) & 140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, filed for the petitioners and against the respondents as mentioned in the memo of parties.
FACTS OF THE CASE 1.

Briefly stated, the facts of the case are that on 03.10.2018, at about 10:10 PM, one Vikas Kumar Singh (since deceased) was crossing the road on foot opposite the temple on Loni Road within the jurisdiction of PS Jyoti Nagar.

It has been alleged that a motorcycle bearing registration no.
DL-13SK-8470 (herein referred to as offending vehicle), came at a very high speed and hit the above-said Vikas Kumar Singh with a great force.

It has been further alleged that the offending vehicle was being driven by its driver i.e. respondent no. 1 (R1) herein, in a rash and negligent manner MACT No. 440/19 DAR- Nandani Devi Vs. Salman Khan and Ors.

11.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is tested on the touchstone of principle of preponderance of probabilities.

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The MACT No. 440/19 DAR- Nandani Devi Vs. Salman Khan and Ors.

LIABILITY 23.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.
The respondent no. 1 ie., Salman Khan is the principal tort feasor being driver, while the respondent no. 2 is vicariously liable being the owner of the offending vehicle.
Herein, it is pertinent to note that the offending vehicle i.e. motorcycle was not insured at the time of the accident.

Furthermore,
though it has been contended by the LR's of the R2 that the latter had already sold off the offending vehicle prior to the accident, but neither such fact has been placed on record nor any details of such subsequent purchases have been furnished on record during the entire course of proceedings.
Hence, on the basis of entire above stated facts and circumstances and discussion of evidence, this Tribunal is of the view that respondent no.1 i.e. driver and R2 i.e. registered owner are jointly and severally liable to pay the entire compensation to the petitioners.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is tested on the touchstone of principle of preponderance of probabilities.
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The MACT No. 440/19 DAR- Nandani Devi Vs. Salman Khan and Ors.
2025.05.03 16:45:42 +0530 burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs Amir Chand & Ors, 2011 (1) SCR 1906 (Civil Appeal No. 1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. ltd. &
Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

Salman Khan and Ors.

On the basis of findings upon issue no. (i), it is clear that the incident in question had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by R-1 and fatal injuries had been caused to the deceased in the incident.
Hence, the petitioners being the wife and parents are entitled to MACT No. 440/19 DAR- Nandani Devi Vs. Salman Khan and Ors.
Furthermore,
though it has been contended by the LR's of the R2 that the latter had already sold off the offending vehicle prior to the accident, but neither such fact has been placed on record nor any details of such subsequent purchases have been furnished on record during the entire course of proceedings.
Hence, on the basis of entire above stated facts and circumstances and discussion of evidence, this Tribunal is of the view that respondent no.1 i.e. driver and R2 i.e. registered owner are jointly and severally liable to pay the entire compensation to the petitioners.
It is clear from above stated facts and circumstances that the deceased died on 06.10.2018 three days after the accident, while he was treated for his injuries at government hospitals and no medical expenditure was undertaken by the petitioners in the treatment of the deceased before his death.
Hence, petitioners are not entitled to any compensation under this head on account of absence of any evidence brought on record in this regard.

per month.
Therefore, in absence of any documents filed on record to show that deceased used to earn Rs. 20,000/-,

It has been brought on record by the petitioners that the deceased Vikas was married and having his wife and parents as dependent upon him on the date of the incident, while no material record has been brought on record to show that the brother of the deceased arrayed as petitioner no. 03 in the present case was dependent upon the deceased in any manner.
